facts.raw_span: sinus rhythm with diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR
elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle
6.3 cm×4.5 cm×5.5 cm cystic mass above the left atrium
sinus rhythm with diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR
elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle
6.3 cm×4.5 cm×5.5 cm cystic mass above the left atrium

concepts.why: The presence of a large cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and the development of transient cardiogenic shock suggest cardiac tamponade.

The electrocardiogram showing sinus rhythm with diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR, along with an elevated cardiac troponin I level, is consistent with acute coronary syndrome.
The presence of chest and back pain, diffuse ST-segment depression, and a cystic mass above the left atrium suggests pericarditis.
The elevated cardiac troponin I level and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle are consistent with myocardial infarction.
The history of hypertension and the presence of diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle suggest hypertensive heart disease.

rationales.F05: ST elevation in lead aVR is concerning for pericarditis or myocardial infarction.
rationales.F06: Elevated troponin levels are indicative of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F08: A large cystic mass above the left atrium is suggestive of a pericardial cyst or other cardiac tamponade cause.
rationales.F10: Transient cardiogenic shock is a serious complication that can occur in several cardiac conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large cystic mass above the left atrium and subsequent development of transient cardiogenic shock, which responded to noradrenaline support, strongly supports Cardiac Tamponade as the primary diagnosis, despite some findings also suggestive of Acute Coronary Syndrome.
